stemEn: A child has habitual snoring and excessive daytime sleepiness, raising concern for obstructive sleep apnea. What is the next diagnostic test?
explanationAr: المصدر يختار Polysomnography. يذكر أن attended overnight PSG هو gold standard لتشخيص obstructive sleep apnea لأنه يحدد obstructive events ويقيس شدة المرض واضطراب gas exchange وsleep arousals.
reasoningEn: The source identifies attended overnight polysomnography as the definitive diagnostic study for suspected pediatric obstructive sleep apnea.
clinicalPearl: Habitual snoring plus daytime sleepiness should prompt formal evaluation for pediatric OSA; the source names PSG as the gold standard.

tts.text: A child has habitual snoring and excessive daytime sleepiness, raising concern for obstructive sleep apnea. What is the next diagnostic test? Option A, polysomnography.

sourceRefs.notes: Part II 2022 and Part II 2020; source answer A.

verification.referenceNotes: Source explanation states attended overnight PSG is the gold standard.

stemEn: A 5-year-old wakes frightened during the night. Which feature would support nightmares?

options.text: They occur in the first third of sleep
They are not associated with other abnormalities

explanationAr: المصدر يختار حدوث nightmares خلال REM sleep. هذا هو التفريق الذي يركز عليه السؤال بين nightmares وبين parasomnias الأخرى التي قد ترتبط بمراحل نوم مختلفة.
reasoningEn: The source-selected distinguishing feature is occurrence during REM sleep.
incorrectOptionsAr: المصدر لا يقدم شرحًا تفصيليًا مستقلًا لكل خيار في هذه الفقرة، لذلك لم تُضف استبعادات غير مذكورة.
clinicalPearl: In the source, REM timing is the key clue for nightmares.

tts.text: A 5-year-old wakes frightened during the night. Which feature would support nightmares? Option A, they occur during REM sleep. Option B, they occur in the first third of sleep. Option C, they are not associated with other abnormalities. Option D, they do not affect sleep.

sourceRefs.sourceName: Pediatric Saudi Board Exams Question Collection, 4th Edition, 1 May 2026
sourceRefs.notes: Part II 2022 and Part II 2021; source answer A.

stemEn: A child goes to sleep at 8 p.m. and wakes crying at about 4 to 5 a.m.; no additional description was recalled. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanationAr: مفتاح المصدر مطبوع A? ويذكر أن الترجيح كان فقط لأن الحدث وقع في مرحلة متأخرة من النوم. الـrecall ناقص ولا يحتوي وصف الحلم أو الوعي أو amnesia أو autonomic activation، لذلك لا تُحوّل الإجابة إلى verified.
reasoningEn: The source tentatively favors nightmares based only on late-night timing, while explicitly acknowledging that the recalled vignette lacks discriminating details.
incorrectOptionsAr: لا توجد تفاصيل كافية في الـrecall لاستبعاد sleep terrors أو confusional arousals بصورة موثوقة؛ لذلك بقي السؤال conflicting.
clinicalPearl: Timing alone is insufficient for a confident parasomnia diagnosis when key behavioral features are missing.

stemEn: A child has difficulty falling asleep and requires a specific soothing condition throughout the night, such as being swaddled. What is the probable cause?
explanationAr: المصدر يختار Behavioral insomnia of childhood ويشرح sleep-onset association type: الطفل يجد صعوبة في النوم أو العودة للنوم دون conditions أو associations محددة مثل rocking أو وجود parent أو favorite object.
reasoningEn: The source maps dependence on a specific bedtime condition to the sleep-onset association form of behavioral insomnia of childhood.
incorrectOptionsAr: المصدر لا يربط هذا النمط بـdepression أو night terrors؛ المحور هو dependence on a sleep-onset association.
clinicalPearl: A child who cannot fall back asleep without the same bedtime association fits the source description of sleep-onset association insomnia.
